mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of 2% or more signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: No statistically significant negative correlation (p > 0.05) between GDPC1 YoY < -2% and subsequent 60-day S&P 500 returns.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during periods when UNRATE exceeds 6% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of 1% or more for three consecutive months signals contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces earnings for industrial firms and drags the S&P 500 lower over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls for three consecutive months by at least 1% each month
failure_condition: No significant negative correlation (p > 0.05) between INDPRO 3-month decline and subsequent 20-day S&P 500 returns.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and core CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 3% signals a dual monetary and inflationary shock, which increases real interest rates and erodes equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 3% AND CPIAUCSL > 3% in the same month
failure_condition: No significant negative correlation (p > 0.05) between the joint FEDFUNDS > 3% and CPIAUCSL > 3% event and subsequent 60-day S&P 500 returns.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly decline in housing starts (HOUST) of more than 10% from the previous month signals a collapse in residential investment, which negatively impacts construction and related sectors and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) following a month with HOUST decline >10%.

mechanism_narrative: A positive and accelerating change in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) growth (i.e., month-over-month change in PAYEMS increases from previous month) signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: Month-over-month change in PAYEMS accelerates (second derivative > 0)
failure_condition: No significant positive correlation (p > 0.05) between accelerating PAYEMS growth and subsequent 20-day S&P 500 returns.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a broad-based demand contraction, which reduces corporate revenue and profit expectations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both fall by >1% month-over-month
failure_condition: No significant negative correlation (p > 0.05) between joint GDPC1 and HOUST monthly declines >1% and subsequent 20-day S&P 500 returns.
